title: Core
description: The seven kinds every type extends, the root relations every relation extends, and the system tier.

types.title: Actor
types.description: Holds authority, owns work and is waited on: a person, a company, an agent. One of the seven kinds every type extends.

types.title: Aim
types.description: Why work exists: what serves points at, such as a goal or an area. One of the seven kinds every type extends.

types.title: Work
types.description: Open until finished; it blocks and is blocked: a task, a project, an issue. One of the seven kinds every type extends.

types.title: Question
types.description: Open until settled, by someone's word or by evidence: a decision, a hypothesis, an idea. One of the seven kinds every type extends.

types.title: Record
types.description: Explains, and is replaced by a newer one: a note, a result, a procedure, a document. One of the seven kinds every type extends.

types.title: Occurrence
types.description: Happens at a time, and can be a gate: an event, a meeting, a release. One of the seven kinds every type extends.

types.title: Place
types.description: Exists somewhere, physical or not; work lives in it or uses it: a resource, a repository, a file. One of the seven kinds every type extends.

role.description: What they do, in a few words.

types.title: Company
types.description: An organisation: a business, client, vendor or institution.

types.title: Agent
types.description: A non-human actor with its own identity, such as an AI agent or an automation.

kind.description: What sort of agent, e.g. claude-code.

types.title: Goal
types.description: An outcome that projects and tasks serve.

measure.description: How you will know it is achieved.

types.title: Area
types.description: An ongoing responsibility with no end date.

types.title: Event
types.description: Something that happens at a time: a deadline, a launch, an appointment.

types.title: Resource
types.description: Something limited or exclusive that work needs: a machine, a licence, a budget, a live app.

exclusive.description: If true, only one holder at a time; everything else that needs it is blocked.

types.title: Lens
types.description: What is in a picture of the map. About a project or item, it is a view of that thing, named by its title: an item's page shows its views as a switch and opens on the first (place). About nothing, it is the workspace's: a view that can be chosen for any picture, and the one the whole map opens on. A field left empty is the built-in one. Read by the lens view.

place.description: Its order among the views of the item it is about: the lowest is the one the page opens on.

pinned.description: Kept in sight by the owner: shown on Home and first in the Atlas.

from.description: The id of the item this view starts from, when that is not the item it is about. Such a view is a shortcut: the page shows it as a way to that item.

controls.description: What the person looking may change on the page, as a list of: lit (what stays lit), far (how many steps down), closed (whether what is finished shows). None when not set.

kinds.description: Types to keep, as a list: a type (flavours included) or "work"; with a leading "-", to leave out.

by.description: The kind of link that says what is inside what, e.g. part_of.

over.description: The kinds of link sent along as links, as a list, or "all".

far.description: How many steps down from the start.

lanes.description: What each item is filed under: stage, link, person, or field:<name> for the value of one of its fields (e.g. field:phase).

order.description: The number field that orders things beside each other.

fold.description: What is left out, as a list of: closed, system, unlinked.

time.description: A time axis: {from, to} as dates or date-times, and by: ["when", "bound"] if not both. Only what falls in the window is in the picture, each item with its spans (time).

types.title: Style
types.description: How a picture of the map is drawn. About a project or item, it is how that thing's picture looks; about nothing, the workspace's. A field left empty comes from the level above. Read only by the page that draws.

shape.description: One of the drawings that come built in, used when the style has no code of its own. architecture: a system read from the top down, each part a box (a store a cylinder, a client a pill) inside a box for the place it is part of (a host, a cloud), wires at right angles from a part to what it depends on or calls, each labelled with what the link says; a dot for each part's health (read from its status: up, degraded, down, being wired, planned), and each wire wired, not yet wired (dashed) or broken (red), by the link's own state or else by its two ends. list: a table, one line a row, its marks in columns; a thing that holds others a group that folds. grid: rows by what the start holds, columns by the lens's lanes, each thing a card; no lines are drawn. time: along a time axis (the lens's time), as a calendar of days with hours down (layout: calendar) or as bars across days (layout: bars, a Gantt chart), each lane a row; the one a lens on a time axis is drawn in unless said. flow: a process map read from the top down, each item a step (work a box, a question a diamond, an occurrence a pill, a record a sheet), wires at right angles from what is depended on to what depends on it, an open question's choices as dashed scenarios. Any other look is code of its own. list unless said.

lit.description: What stays lit as it opens.

layout.description: time: a calendar of days, hours running down (calendar), or each lane a row of bars across the days (bars, a Gantt chart). calendar unless said.

hours.description: time, calendar: the hours of the day shown, as [from, to], e.g. [6, 22]. The whole day unless said.

open.description: list: how many levels are open as it first draws.

show.description: list: the columns each row has, as a list of: type, status, waits, sessions. status, waits and sessions unless said.

column.description: The least width of a box, in pixels.

text.description: The size of names, in pixels.

radius.description: How round corners are, in pixels.

gap.description: The room between things, in pixels.

colors.description: Colours by name, each a hex colour: sea, land, inner, line, text, muted, blocked, you, session, done.

color_by.description: grid: the shown field each card is coloured by, e.g. kind.

rows.description: grid: what the rows are. Left empty, what the start holds. link:<kind>, the things those links lead to, e.g. link:funding.could_fund: a thing is a card in each row its links lead to, with the link's words as its second line.

palette.description: grid: a hex colour for each value of color_by, e.g. {"grant": "#2e7d4f"}. A value not named takes one of the built-in colours.

labels.description: grid: what a lane or a value is called, e.g. {"set_up": "Set up"}. Not named, it is the value in words.

detail.description: grid: the shown field written on each card's second line, e.g. amount.

mark.description: grid: the shown date field marked on a card, with the field <name>_note before it when there is one, e.g. deadline.

code.description: The drawing itself, as a JavaScript module: export default function draw({ canvas, answer, style, theme, size, tree, three, on, open, tip, cursor }). It runs in the browser of whoever looks, in a worker inside a sandboxed frame: it has a canvas to draw on and no page, no network and no storage. Written by an agent, it waits for the human to approve it before it runs. canvas is an OffscreenCanvas (2D or WebGL); answer is what the lens view answered; style is this style's other fields; theme is the page's colours (sea, land, inner, line, text, muted, blocked, you, session, done) and dark; size is { width, height, dpr }, kept current; tree() gives the answer as a tree ({ root, byId, me }, each thing with kids, up, depth and its counts all, work, blk, you, at); three() resolves to three.js; on(name, fn) hears pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup, pointerleave, wheel (each { x, y, button, buttons, deltaY, shift, ctrl }) and resize; open(id) opens an item's page; tip(text, x, y) shows words by the pointer (null hides them); cursor(name) sets the pointer. With code, shape is not used.

types.title: Screen
types.description: A page the kernel draws as one column of pieces: a picture (a lens in a style), rows from a pack's view, an action's form, an item's fields, a short note. On kinds or types (on), it is shown on the page of every such item; given a place in the nav (nav), it is a page of its own there; on Home (home), it is drawn there after the screens before it. A pack ships screens as presets; one kept on the map with the preset's id (preset) is the owner's version of it, and retired, the preset is not shown. Only a person changes a screen: an agent's change waits for them.

pieces.description: The column, in order: each {piece, ...what it needs}. picture: lens (a lens's id, or the params of the lens view) and style (a style's id, or its fields, code aside); view: view (a pack's view of rows) and item (the input the item's id goes in); action: action (a pack's action); fields: fields (a list of the item's fields); note: text. Left empty, the preset's.

on.description: The kinds or types on whose page it is shown, as a list. Left empty, the preset's.

nav.description: Its place in the nav, after Home and Search: the lowest first. Left empty, it is not in the nav.

home.description: Drawn on Home (true) or taken off it (false). Left empty, the preset's: a pack's screen for Home is on it.

preset.description: The id of the pack's screen this is the owner's version of.

relations.title: depends on
relations.description: The source cannot finish until the target is closed. Drives the blockers view.

relations.title: waits on
relations.description: The source cannot move until this person, company or agent has answered or acted. Say what is awaited in the relation's props.for, as what they are to do, in a few words, said to them: "Choose the pack's name", not "choosing the name". Drives the blockers view; remove the link once they have.

relations.title: goes ahead without
relations.description: The event was planned with this in sight and does not wait for it: it can follow. What the event does wait for is depends_on. Drives the gate view.

relations.title: is part of
relations.description: Hierarchy: a task in a project, a project in an area.

relations.title: works at
relations.description: Put the job title in the relation's props.role.

relations.title: is about
relations.description: A note, file, decision or issue concerns the target.

relations.title: needs
relations.description: The work cannot run without this resource. Drives the blockers view.

relations.title: holds
relations.description: Current occupancy of a resource. Created by claim, ended by release.

relations.title: produced
relations.description: The work led to this result, file or decision.

relations.title: lives in
relations.description: Where something is: work in a repository, a visit at a site.

relations.title: bears on
relations.description: Evidence on a question: a result, a test or a finding that helps settle it.

relations.title: relates to
relations.description: A loose link. Prefer a specific relation when one fits.

verbs.title: Capture
verbs.description: Put something on the map: an item and its links, or a record of what happened.

verbs.title: Assign
verbs.description: Give work to someone, inside the map or outside it: an owner, a person waited on, a party asked to act.

verbs.title: Report
verbs.description: Say that something happened or is so: progress, a result, a payment received, a check that it is still true.

verbs.title: Ask
verbs.description: Put a question to someone and wait for the answer.

verbs.title: Settle
verbs.description: Close a question by someone's word or by evidence: a decision made, a hypothesis borne out.

verbs.title: Revise
verbs.description: Change, correct or undo what is on the map.

rules.say: Code that runs in the browser of whoever looks is the human's to allow.
What a screen shows, and where, is the human's to change.
Folding one style into another can bring its code along: the human's to allow.
What anyone can see is the human's to decide.
